bib.title: Multimodal Few-Shot Learning with Frozen Language Models

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Multimodal Few-Shot Learning with Frozen Language Models", Tsimpoukelli, Menick, Cabi, Eslami, Vinyals, Hill (DeepMind). The file is arXiv 2106.13884v2 (3 Jul 2021), and its footer reads "Preprint. Under review." It is the pre-NeurIPS camera-ready version, so check the NeurIPS 2021 citation against the venue version.
PDF: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/ai-engineering/08-multimodal-engineering/sources/tsimpoukelli-2021-multimodal-few-shot-learning-frozen.pdf

COVERAGE: I read all 19 pages (61,630 of 61,630 chars), including appendices A.1–A.5 and Figs 5–11. I only skimmed the references (pp.10–12).

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. **Architecture: the image becomes a few soft tokens through a linear map.** NF-ResNet-50 produces a pooled output vector. A linear layer maps it to D·n channels, which are reshaped into n embeddings of the LM's token dimension. They tried n = 1, 2 and 4, and 2 worked best. Only the vision encoder is trained. The 7B LM stays frozen, and gradients pass back through it.
   - Setup: 7B GPT-like LM trained on C4 (32 layers, d=4096). Training data is Conceptual Captions, about 3M image-caption pairs, at 224×224.
   - Quote: "we tried 1, 2 and 4 and found that 2 performs best, though certainly this would be sensitive to other architectural details". The text actually reads "We experimented using different number of tokens, speciﬁcally 1, 2 and 4 and found that 2 performs best…" (p.4).
2. **Zero-shot to few-shot VQA (Table 1, VQAv2 val, 7B LM, trained on captions only).**
   - Frozen scores 29.5 / 35.7 / 38.2 at n = 0 / 1 / 4.
   - The blind baseline scores 26.2 / 33.5 / 33.3.
   - Fine-tuning the LM gives 24.0 / 28.2 / 29.2.
   - Training from scratch gives 0.0.
   - Adding VQAv2 training data gives 48.4. Oscar (SOTA) gives 73.8.
   - Quote: "goes a decent way toward closing the gap from zero-shot performance (29.5%) to full SGD training performance (48.4%). With just four examples the gap is closed almost halfway at 38.2%." (p.7)
3. **Freezing the LM beats fine-tuning it.** Quote: "Our experiments show that ﬁne-tuning θ hurts generalization, as much less paired image-caption data is available than the amount of text-only data used to pre-train θ." (p.4) Table 1 supports this, and so does Table 2 (OKVQA: fine-tuned 4.2 / 4.1 / 4.6 vs frozen 5.9 / 9.7 / 12.6).
4. **Outside knowledge grows with LM size (Table 2, OKVQA, never trained on).** The 7B LM scores 5.9 / 9.7 / 12.6 at 0 / 1 / 4 shots. The 400M LM scores 4.0 / 5.9 / 6.6. The task-trained SOTA (MAVEx) scores 39.4. Quote: "Table 2 shows the results: task performance scales with model size." (p.7)
5. **Fast binding works 2-way but fails 5-way (Tables 3–4, Open-Ended miniImageNet).**
   - In the 2-way task, chance is 50%. Frozen goes from 53.4 to 58.9 as inner-shots rise from 1 to 5 (with task induction). The ANIL baseline scores 73.9–84.2.
   - In the 5-way task, chance is 20%. Frozen scores 18.0–22.3.
   - Quote: "Frozen is not signiﬁcantly above chance" (p.8).

QUOTES worth using in the note
- "a sequence of continuous embeddings, each having the same dimensionality D as a token embedding t_l … We call this sequence a visual preﬁx since it plays the same functional role in the transformer architecture as (part of) an embedding sequence of preﬁx tokens." (p.4)
- "Because the transformer fθ is modality-agnostic, we can interleave a sub-sequence of text token embeddings with a sub-sequence of image embeddings in any arbitrary order." (p.5)
- "Frozen could also be considered a type of image-conditional preﬁx tuning, in which this continuous prompt is not a bias but an image-conditional activation produced by an external neural network." (p.3)

LIMITS
- The authors concede it is "far from state-of-the-art performance on the speciﬁc tasks that it learns in a few shots" and call it a "proof-of-concept" (p.9).
- They did not explore more elaborate vision-language mixing architectures.
- Fast binding fails 5-way.
- Qualitative samples are curated. The Fig 1/9 captions say about 5 seeds were needed, and A.5 says it "can require 3-4 tries."
- The blind baseline is close to Frozen on VQAv2, so the LM prior does much of the work.
- The image is a single pooled vector turned into 2 tokens, with no patch grid. Later VLMs such as LLaVA feed in per-patch features, so the "few tokens per image" detail is dated.
- The model is trained only on single image-caption pairs. Multi-image interleaving works through relative position encoding but was never trained.
- The new benchmarks were promised "with the camera ready version" and were not released in this version.

BUILDS ON
- Prefix-tuning (Li & Liang 2021) and prompt tuning (Lester et al. 2021).
- Pretrained transformers as universal computation engines (Lu et al. 2021).
- GPT-3 few-shot learning (Brown et al. 2020).
- NF-ResNet (Brock et al. 2021).
- Relative position encodings (Shaw et al. 2018).
- Conceptual Captions (Sharma et al. 2018).
- CLIP (Radford et al. 2021) and ALIGN (Jia et al. 2021), both cited as discriminative contrast.
- VisualGPT (Chen et al. 2021).
- Matching networks / miniImageNet (Vinyals et al. 2016).

FIGURE candidate: Fig 2, p.2, "Gradients through a frozen language model's self attention layers are used to train the vision encoder." It shows in one picture what the note says in prose. The vision encoder's output goes into the same slot as the text embedder's output, and only the vision encoder is trained. That is the "image features as if they were words" idea one step before LLaVA's projector. Fig 3 (p.2, the interleaved inference interface) is an alternative.

PROBLEMS
- Equations and figure text come out fragmented, but the prose and tables are readable.
- Small extraction quirks: "minImageNet" (sic), and the ligature "ﬁ" appears in quotes.
- The tick/cross marks in the tables' τ and "Task Induction" rows did not extract. I inferred which columns use task induction from the prose and column layout, so check Table 3/4 headers against the PDF.
- No embedded instructions.
